meta.title: Manoeuvring and position on the carriageway
meta.summary: You will learn how to signal, change lanes, turn, make U-turns and reverse correctly. You will find out which lane to use on different roads and what following distance to keep.

p: Every manoeuvre starts with a signal: this way others understand in advance what you are going to do. Signals are given with the direction indicators or, if there are none or they are faulty, by hand. The manoeuvre itself must be safe and must not impede others ⟦18⟧.
In the Rules, a manoeuvre is not only a turn. Moving off from a standstill, stopping, changing lanes, braking and reversing also count as manoeuvring ⟦19⟧.
list: Left: the left direction indicator, or the left arm extended to the side, or the right arm extended to the side and bent upwards at the elbow at a right angle.
Right: the right direction indicator, or the right arm extended to the side, or the left arm extended to the side and bent upwards at the elbow at a right angle.
Braking: the brake lights or a raised arm. Reversing: the reversing lights and the hazard warning lights.
A signal is given in good time and in a way that does not mislead others, and it is cancelled immediately after the manoeuvre. A hand signal may be ended immediately before the manoeuvre ⟦20⟧.
lesson.tip: A signal is a warning, not a right. It does not give you priority or release you from taking precautions ⟦21⟧.

lesson.h: Entering and leaving a road, yards, acceleration and deceleration lanes
list: When pulling out from a minor road onto a road, give way to vehicles and pedestrians moving along the road you are entering ⟦22⟧.
A dirt road is a minor road in relation to a paved road, even if there are no signs ⟦23⟧.
When leaving a residential zone or a yard, give way to all other road users ⟦24⟧.
When leaving a road, give way to vehicles and pedestrians whose path you cross ⟦25⟧.
When approaching a place to stop or park, give way to pedestrians, cyclists, drivers of mopeds and horse-drawn carts, and drovers moving along the edge of the carriageway or on the shoulder ⟦26⟧.
If there is a deceleration lane, move into it in good time and slow down only in that lane ⟦27⟧.
If there is an acceleration lane, drive along it and move into the adjacent lane, giving way to vehicles travelling on the road ⟦28⟧.

p: When you change lanes, you move into another stream of traffic. That is why those driving straight on in their own lane have priority.
list: Give way to vehicles travelling in the same direction that are not changing lanes ⟦29⟧.
If you and a vehicle alongside change lanes at the same time, the driver who has the other vehicle on the right gives way ⟦30⟧.
You must not change lanes in a way that leaves a dangerous distance between vehicles ⟦31⟧.
If the lanes are marked, keep strictly to them. You may drive over broken marking lines only when changing lanes ⟦32⟧.
If paths cross and the Rules do not specify who goes first, the driver who has the other vehicle approaching from the right gives way ⟦33⟧.
lesson.tip: When vehicles change lanes at the same time, the driver with the other vehicle on the right gives way.

p: Before turning right or left or making a U-turn, take up the appropriate far right or far left position on the carriageway in advance ⟦34⟧. The exception is a turn made when entering a roundabout.
Turn in such a way that, on leaving the intersection of the carriageways, you do not end up on the side for oncoming traffic ⟦35⟧.
list: If signs 5.8.1 or 5.8.2 are installed, turn from the lanes they permit. However, you must not take an inner lane while the far lane on the side of the turn is free ⟦36⟧.

If there are tram tracks for the same direction on the left, level with the road, and signs 5.8.1 or 5.8.2 do not set lane directions, you turn left and make U-turns from the tram tracks, giving way to trams ⟦37⟧.

If your vehicle cannot turn from the far right or far left position because of its dimensions, you may move partly or completely into the adjacent lane, provided this is safe and does not impede anyone ⟦38⟧.

p: The arrows of marking 1.18 and signs 5.8.1 and 5.8.2 show which way you may go from each lane. If the arrow in your lane points straight ahead only, you must not turn from that lane, even when the adjacent lane is free.

A turn is made into the lane that corresponds to the one you occupy (para. 53, in force since 6 May 2024): from the far right lane into the far right lane, from the far left into the far left, from the second into the second. You may change lanes once the turn is complete. A special case is turning onto a road with reversible traffic: there you take the far right lane straight away ⟦39⟧.
list: A left arrow in the far left lane also permits a U-turn from that lane (marking 1.18, signs 5.8.1, 5.8.2).
Does a sign permit turning from several lanes? Do not take an inner lane while the far lane on the side of the turn is free ⟦40⟧.
Marking 1.18 showing a dead end means that turning into the nearest carriageway is prohibited.
lesson.tip: The “lane-to-lane” rule appeared in 2024, so older question banks may not include it.

p: You may make a U-turn with any turning radius, provided it is safe and does not impede others ⟦41⟧. Outside an intersection, when turning left or making a U-turn, give way to oncoming vehicles ⟦42⟧.

If the road is narrow and a U-turn from the far left position is not possible, the U-turn may be made only from the right edge of the carriageway (from the right-hand shoulder), and you give way to vehicles travelling in the same direction as well as to oncoming vehicles ⟦43⟧.
list: on pedestrian crossings, including at intersections along the line of the pavements or shoulders where pedestrians cross (U-turns at the intersection itself are not prohibited, para. 61);
in tunnels;
on bridges, overpasses and flyovers, and under them;
on level crossings;
where visibility of the road is less than 100 m;
at bus (tram) stops.
lesson.tip: On motorways, U-turns, entering service gaps in the central reservation and reversing are prohibited ⟦45⟧. Sign 5.11.1 “U-turn place” shows where you may make a U-turn, but turning left there is prohibited.

p: Visibility is worst to the rear, so reversing is permitted only if it is safe and does not impede others ⟦46⟧. Reversing is signalled by the reversing lights and the hazard warning lights ⟦47⟧.
list: Reversing is prohibited at intersections.

Reversing is prohibited wherever U-turns are prohibited: on pedestrian crossings, in tunnels, on bridges, overpasses and flyovers and under them, on level crossings, where visibility is less than 100 m, and at stops ⟦48⟧.
lesson.tip: Missed the turning you needed at an intersection? Do not reverse: drive on to a place where you can legally make a U-turn.

lesson.h: How many lanes there are and where the oncoming side is
p: The number of lanes is shown by road markings or signs 5.8.1, 5.8.2, 5.8.7 and 5.8.8. If there are none, drivers determine it themselves, taking into account the width of the carriageway, the dimensions of the vehicles and the necessary clearances ⟦49⟧.
The left half of the carriageway is considered the side for oncoming traffic, unless traffic management establishes otherwise. Local widening of the road is not taken into account ⟦50⟧.
list: Two-way traffic, four or more lanes: driving onto the side for oncoming traffic is prohibited. Left turns and U-turns are made at intersections and in other places where they are not prohibited ⟦51⟧.
Two-way traffic, three lanes: driving into the far left lane, which is intended for oncoming traffic, is prohibited ⟦52⟧.
Two-way traffic, two lanes separated by marking 1.1 and (or) marked with sign 3.20: driving onto the oncoming side is prohibited, except in cases provided for by the Rules ⟦53⟧.

p: Kazakhstan has right-hand traffic ⟦54⟧. Outside built-up areas, and also in towns on roads with signs 5.1 and 5.3 or where more than 80 km/h is permitted, keep close to the right edge and do not use the left lanes while the right lanes are free ⟦55⟧.

In built-up areas, you may drive in any lane. But if you are driving in the left lane slower than the permitted speed, and a faster vehicle approaches from behind giving a warning light signal (flashing its headlights by day or switching between dipped and main-beam headlights at night, para. 140), move to the right and free the lane ⟦56⟧.
list: Three or more lanes in one direction: the far left lane is used only in heavy traffic, when the other lanes are occupied, and also for overtaking, turning left or making a U-turn ⟦57⟧.
On such roads, trucks with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3500 kg may use the far left lane only for turning left or making a U-turn ⟦58⟧.
On motorways, trucks with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3500 kg must not drive beyond the second lane ⟦59⟧.

Vehicles that travel at no more than 40 km/h or cannot technically reach that speed keep to the far right lane. Exceptions: driving around an obstacle, overtaking, and changing lanes before turning left, making a U-turn or making a permitted stop on the left-hand side ⟦60⟧.
Driving in your own lane faster than vehicles in the adjacent lane is not overtaking ⟦61⟧, so sign 3.20 does not prohibit it.

lesson.h: Tram tracks, shoulders and obstacles in the middle of the road
list: You may drive on tram tracks for the same direction, on the left and level with the road, when all lanes are occupied, and also when driving around an obstacle, overtaking, turning left or making a U-turn. You must not impede trams ⟦62⟧.
You must not drive onto tram tracks for the oncoming direction. If signs 5.8.1 or 5.8.2 are installed, you must not drive through the intersection on the tram tracks ⟦63⟧.

Driving on shoulders, pavements and footpaths is prohibited, and in built-up areas driving off the carriageway, for example on lawns, is prohibited too. Exceptions: road maintenance and utility vehicles, and vehicles delivering goods that approach by the shortest route when there is no other access ⟦64⟧.
Traffic islands, bollards and bridge supports in the middle of a road without a central reservation are driven around on the right, unless signs and markings require otherwise ⟦65⟧.
Having turned onto a road with reversible traffic, take the far right lane. Change lanes only after making sure that driving in your direction is also permitted in the other lanes ⟦66⟧.

p: The following distance is the distance to the vehicle in front. Keep a distance that lets you avoid a collision if it brakes sharply. The higher the speed, the greater the distance you need. The lateral clearance to vehicles alongside must also be safe ⟦67⟧.

Outside built-up areas, on two-lane roads with two-way traffic, vehicles for which a speed limit has been set, and vehicles or vehicle combinations longer than 7 m, keep enough distance ahead for overtaking vehicles to return to their lane without hindrance. This is not required if the driver is preparing to overtake, in heavy traffic or in an organised convoy ⟦68⟧.
lesson.tip: Paragraph 69 does not give an exact figure in metres: a safe distance depends on the speed and the situation.

keyFacts: A signal is given in good time and cancelled immediately after the manoeuvre; it does not give priority ⟦1⟧.
Right-turn hand signal: the right arm extended to the side, or the left arm bent upwards at the elbow at a right angle; braking: a raised arm ⟦2⟧.
When changing lanes, give way to vehicles travelling in the same direction without changing lanes; when changing lanes at the same time, give way to the one on the right ⟦3⟧.
Before turning or making a U-turn, take up the far right or far left position in advance, and turn into the lane that corresponds to the one you occupy ⟦4⟧.
A left arrow in the far left lane (marking 1.18, signs 5.8.1, 5.8.2) also permits a U-turn.

Outside an intersection, when turning left or making a U-turn, give way to oncoming vehicles; when making a U-turn from the right-hand shoulder, give way both to vehicles travelling in the same direction and to oncoming vehicles ⟦5⟧.
U-turns are prohibited on pedestrian crossings, in tunnels, on bridges, overpasses and flyovers and under them, on level crossings, where visibility is less than 100 m, and at stops ⟦6⟧.
Reversing is prohibited at intersections and wherever U-turns are prohibited; it is signalled by the reversing lights and the hazard warning lights ⟦7⟧.
When leaving a yard or a residential zone, give way to everyone; when pulling out from a dirt road onto a paved road, give way to everyone travelling on it ⟦8⟧.
On a two-way road with 4 or more lanes, driving onto the oncoming side is prohibited; on a three-lane road, you must not use the far left lane ⟦9⟧.
Outside built-up areas and where more than 80 km/h is permitted, keep to the right; for trucks over 3500 kg, the far left of three lanes is only for turning left and making U-turns ⟦10⟧.
Vehicles and vehicle combinations longer than 7 m, and vehicles for which a speed limit has been set, leave room ahead for overtaking vehicles on a two-lane road outside built-up areas ⟦11⟧.
mistakes: Thinking that switching on your indicator gives you the right to change lanes. A signal does not give priority: give way to those driving straight on in the lane ⟦12⟧.
Turning right directly into the second lane, or turning left into the right lane. A turn is made into the lane that corresponds to the one you occupy ⟦13⟧.
Reversing at an intersection after overshooting your turning. Reversing at intersections is prohibited ⟦14⟧.
Making a U-turn on or under a bridge, at a stop or on a stretch where visibility is less than 100 m. All of this is prohibited ⟦15⟧.
Driving in the left lane of an out-of-town highway while the right lane is free. Outside built-up areas, you must keep to the right ⟦16⟧.
Driving around a traffic jam on the shoulder. Driving on shoulders is prohibited, except in cases expressly specified in the Rules ⟦17⟧.
